description: Julien Royer's flagship at the National Gallery is Singapore's most globally visible fine-dining room, combining French technique with a refined Asian sensibility. The pale, art-filled dining room, deep wine program and precise service make it a natural first choice for international luxury diners.
highlights: Three-star modern French tasting menu in the National Gallery, with World and Asia 50 Best recognition.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; The World's 50 Best Restaurants; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; La Liste; 50 Best Discovery; Official website

description: Les Amis remains one of Singapore's defining luxury restaurants, with classical French cooking, a polished Orchard Road room and one of Asia's landmark wine cellars. It is the city's grand old guard: formal, exacting and deeply relevant for affluent diners seeking old-world assurance.
highlights: Three-star French institution with a grand cellar, discreet service and longstanding luxury status.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; La Liste; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Seroja has become one of Singapore's most important contemporary restaurants by translating the Malay Archipelago into a poised, highly personal tasting menu. Its Bugis dining room is understated but serious, with sustainability, regional produce and narrative-driven cooking at the center of the experience.
highlights: Michelin-starred and Asia 50 Best-ranked modern Malay Archipelago tasting menu with strong sustainability credentials.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Restaurant Born occupies a dramatic heritage building and stages Zor Tan's contemporary Chinese-inflected tasting menu with real theatre. The room, service cadence and chef pedigree give it the scale and polish expected of a destination restaurant.
highlights: Asia 50 Best-ranked and Michelin-starred contemporary restaurant in a striking former rickshaw depot.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Rishi Naleendra's Cloudstreet is one of Singapore's most distinctive two-star restaurants, blending Australian technique, Sri Lankan memory and Southeast Asian ingredients. The room feels intimate and modern, while the beverage pairings and pacing make it a confident special-occasion choice.
highlights: Two-star tasting menu with Australian-Sri Lankan roots, polished pairings and intimate service.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; La Liste; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Meta is a sleek two-star restaurant where Korean chef Sun Kim brings Korean flavors into a modern European and Asian tasting-menu framework. Its Keong Saik-adjacent setting, mature service and consistent critical reputation keep it among the city's most reliable fine-dining bookings.
highlights: Two-star Korean-influenced contemporary tasting menu with Asia 50 Best extended-list recognition.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 51-100; La Liste; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Thevar reframes Indian flavors through a polished, modern tasting-menu format that feels both vivid and luxurious. Its two-star status, intimate room and spice-driven precision make it one of Singapore's most compelling alternatives to French or Japanese fine dining.
highlights: Two-star modern Indian tasting menu with serious spice work, premium ingredients and high-energy service.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 51-100; La Liste; Official website

description: Perched high above the city, JAAN by Kirk Westaway turns modern British cooking into a polished Singapore skyline experience. It suits affluent diners who want both culinary ambition and a memorable room, with views, service and wine working together.
highlights: Two-star modern British restaurant with a high-floor skyline setting and luxury hotel polish.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; Black Pearl Restaurant Guide; Official website

description: Saint Pierre is a veteran of Singapore fine dining, pairing Emmanuel Stroobant's contemporary French cooking with a Marina Bay waterfront panorama. Its longevity, two Michelin stars and grown-up service culture make it a classic luxury choice.
highlights: Two-star contemporary French dining room at One Fullerton with Marina Bay views.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Les Grandes Tables du Monde; Official website

description: Shoukouwa is one of Singapore's benchmark sushi counters, built around Toyosu-sourced seafood, omakase discipline and a hushed One Fullerton setting. It offers the kind of intimate, high-spend Japanese experience that affluent diners often book in place of Western fine dining.
highlights: Two-star Edomae-style sushi counter with Toyosu sourcing and an intimate waterfront location.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; La Liste; 50 Best Discovery; Official website

description: Sushi Sakuta rose quickly into Singapore's two-star tier, serving a serene omakase in a room anchored by a 200-year-old cypress counter. The experience is quiet, precise and deeply suited to diners who prize craft, sourcing and restraint.
highlights: Newly promoted two-star sushi omakase with a refined counter and strong chef-owner identity.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website

description: Labyrinth is Singapore's leading modern-national dining statement, reworking local dishes, hawker memories and regional produce into a refined tasting menu. Its location near the Esplanade makes it especially useful for visitors who want a polished yet unmistakably Singaporean dinner.
highlights: Michelin-starred and Asia 50 Best-ranked modern Singaporean tasting menu rooted in local food memory.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; 50 Best Discovery; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Burnt Ends translates wood-fired Australian barbecue into a Michelin-starred, high-energy Dempsey Hill restaurant. It is less formal than the city's tasting-menu temples but equally bookable for affluent diners who want smoke, wine and a confident social room.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern Australian barbecue at Dempsey Hill with a custom brick kiln and boutique wines.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 51-100; 50 Best Discovery; Official website

description: Tetsuya Wakuda's Waku Ghin remains one of Marina Bay Sands' great luxury dining rooms, combining Japanese produce, Western technique and resort-level service. Its private-room progression and polished bar make it an obvious special-occasion choice for international guests.
highlights: Michelin-starred Japanese-European omakase inside Marina Bay Sands with premium seafood and resort polish.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Black Pearl Restaurant Guide; Marina Bay Sands; Official website

description: Nae:um brings contemporary Seoul cuisine to Singapore through episodic menus that balance Korean heritage with Western technique. Its small Telok Ayer dining room feels personal and polished, with enough culinary identity to stand apart in the city's tasting-menu field.
highlights: Michelin-starred and Asia 50 Best-ranked contemporary Korean restaurant with episodic menus.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Asia's 50 Best Restaurants; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Nouri is a cerebral but warmly hosted restaurant built around Ivan Brehm's cross-cultural approach to ingredients and flavor memory. The counter-facing room and serious wine program give it the feel of a chef's workshop made luxurious.
highlights: Michelin-starred cross-cultural tasting menu with a strong intellectual concept and polished hospitality.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; 50 Best Discovery; Official website

description: Candlenut is essential Singapore dining because it elevates Peranakan cooking into a Michelin-starred, design-conscious Dempsey experience. Malcolm Lee's kitchen keeps the cuisine rooted in heritage while making it relevant to international luxury travelers.
highlights: Michelin-starred Peranakan restaurant at COMO Dempsey, balancing heritage flavors and polished service.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; 50 Best Discovery; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Pangium gives Straits cuisine a highly refined setting inside The Orangery at the Singapore Botanic Gardens. Malcolm Lee's tasting menu uses research, memory and regional ingredients to create a distinctly Singaporean luxury dinner surrounded by greenery.
highlights: Michelin-starred Straits cuisine tasting menu in the Botanic Gardens with 180-degree garden views.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; COMO Group; Black Pearl Restaurant Guide; Official website

description: Willow is a compact, contemporary tasting-menu restaurant where Nicolas Tam cooks through a Singaporean lens without locking the food to one tradition. The counter-forward setup and premium seasonal ingredients give it a modern, less-starchy kind of Michelin polish.
highlights: Michelin-starred pan-Asian tasting menu on Hongkong Street with a chef-counter feel.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Hamamoto is an intimate sushi-kappo counter led by chef Kazuhiro Hamamoto after decades of work across Kyoto, Tokyo and Singapore. It suits diners who want Japanese precision with a slightly broader kappo rhythm than a pure nigiri sequence.
highlights: Michelin-starred 12-seat sushi-kappo counter on Tras Street with chef-led hospitality.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; 50 Best Discovery; Culinary Arts Group; Official website

description: Iggy's has long appealed to Singapore's serious wine and fine-dining crowd, with a compact room and a cellar that gives it uncommon depth. The food is modern and international, but the real signature is the balance of culinary maturity and sommelier-led hospitality.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern-contemporary restaurant with a major Burgundy-led cellar and intimate Orchard setting.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website; voco Orchard Singapore

description: Buona Terra offers Italian fine dining in an elegant Scotts Road setting, with premium ingredients, polished service and a romantic pace. It is a strong choice for diners seeking a quieter, European luxury dinner away from the Marina Bay circuit.
highlights: Michelin-starred contemporary Italian restaurant near Orchard with refined service and a special-occasion feel.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Top 50 Italy; Official website

description: CUT remains Singapore's defining luxury steakhouse, combining American chophouse confidence with Marina Bay Sands scale. The room, cocktails, wine list and steak program make it a credible high-end alternative for guests who do not want a tasting menu.
highlights: Michelin-starred luxury steakhouse in Marina Bay Sands with a polished international crowd.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; 50 Best Discovery; Marina Bay Sands; Official website

description: Summer Pavilion is one of Singapore's benchmark Cantonese hotel restaurants, pairing polished Chinese cooking with the calm service culture of The Ritz-Carlton. It is especially relevant for business dinners, family celebrations and guests who want luxury without a Western tasting menu.
highlights: Michelin-starred Cantonese dining room at The Ritz-Carlton with refined service and a serious seafood program.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; Black Pearl Restaurant Guide; Official website

description: Summer Palace brings old-school Cantonese luxury to Conrad Singapore Orchard, with a room suited to discreet celebrations and polished corporate dining. The cooking is refined rather than flashy, making it a useful high-end Chinese anchor in the Orchard luxury-hotel belt.
highlights: Michelin-starred Cantonese restaurant in Conrad Singapore Orchard, with formal service and classic luxury appeal.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Imperial Treasure's Orchard fine Teochew room is a serious Chinese luxury address rather than a casual group concept. The seafood, braises and service rhythm make it a natural choice for affluent local families, business hosts and visitors seeking regional Chinese refinement.
highlights: Michelin-starred Teochew fine dining in ION Orchard with polished seafood and banquet-level service.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website

description: Marguerite uses the Flower Dome at Gardens by the Bay to create one of Singapore's most atmospheric fine-dining settings. Chef Michael Wilson's contemporary tasting menu is elegant, produce-led and well matched to the botanical surroundings.
highlights: Michelin-starred contemporary restaurant inside the Flower Dome, with a rare garden conservatory setting.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Araya is Singapore's rare Chilean fine-dining statement, layering South American heritage with Japanese ingredients and a luxury tasting-menu format. Its Mondrian Duxton setting gives it design relevance as well as culinary novelty.
highlights: Michelin-starred Chilean-Japanese tasting menu in the Mondrian Duxton with strong design appeal.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Tatler Asia; Culinary Arts Group; Official website

description: Omakase @ Stevens adds a newly Michelin-starred Japanese counter to the quiet Stevens Road luxury-hotel corridor. The intimate format, French-inflected kaiseki touches and young-chef momentum make it one of the city's most relevant new high-end Japanese addresses.
highlights: New Michelin one-star omakase restaurant with an intimate counter and French-Japanese seasonal menu.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website

description: Peach Blossoms is a polished Cantonese fine-dining room at PARKROYAL COLLECTION Marina Bay, with skyline views, a refreshed luxury-hotel setting and Asia 50 Best extended-list recognition. It earns its place as a non-starred high-end Chinese alternative to the city's Michelin Cantonese rooms.
highlights: High-end Cantonese restaurant with Marina Bay views and Asia 50 Best 51-100 recognition.
sources: Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 51-100; 50 Best Discovery; Tatler Asia; Official website

description: Kok Sen is a Keong Saik zi char institution whose wok hei, big-prawn hor fun and old-school Chinese dishes remain part of Singapore's shared dining memory. It is informal, but a well-traveled diner can still appreciate the craft, family continuity and local credibility behind the meal.
highlights: Beloved family-run zi char classic with Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition and nearly 50 years of history.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website; The Infatuation

description: Keng Eng Kee is a Bukit Merah seafood and zi char classic that serious local diners still recommend for relaxed group dinners. Its coffee pork ribs, crab and wok-fried dishes make it a culturally grounded counterpoint to Singapore's polished tasting-menu scene.
highlights: Long-running zi char and seafood institution with Michelin selection and chef-loved local status.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website; World of Mouth

description: Sin Huat is a famously idiosyncratic Geylang seafood restaurant, prized for crab bee hoon and direct, no-frills cooking. It is not luxury in decor, but its food culture, late-evening rhythm and seafood prices make it a distinctive relaxed dinner for adventurous affluent diners.
highlights: Geylang seafood classic known for crab bee hoon, no-menu ordering and Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Eater; Local dining guides

description: JUMBO Seafood at Riverside Point is the polished riverfront expression of Singapore's chilli crab tradition. It is a broad local institution rather than a hidden gem, but the sit-down seafood format, setting and signature dishes remain highly useful for visitors seeking a classic Singapore dinner.
highlights: Riverfront seafood institution for chilli crab, black pepper crab and relaxed group dining by the Singapore River.
sources: Official website; MICHELIN Guide; Eater

description: The Blue Ginger has served Peranakan food in a restored Tanjong Pagar shophouse since the mid-1990s. It is a warm, adult and culturally specific local favorite for diners who want heritage cooking without the formality of Candlenut or Pangium.
highlights: Tanjong Pagar Peranakan institution in a restored shophouse, with Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition.
sources: MICHELIN Guide; Official website; Local dining guides
